claims.text: Anatomy-Structured Organ Graph (AOG) constructs an organ-level graph using pre-trained organ segmentations and clinical prior knowledge to model invasion patterns between primary sites and surrounding organs.

claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: AOG addresses the challenge of modeling complex invasion patterns by using pretrained organ segmentations and anatomy-guided connectivity rules to construct an organ-level graph that encodes potential spread between primary sites and surrounding structures.
claims.reason: Section III.A, page 3.

claims.text: Organ-Anchored Cross-Modal Alignment (OCA) performs fine-grained alignment by using each organ node as a query over the radiology report to selectively aggregate relevant textual evidence, enhancing organ features while preserving anatomical topology.
claims.poster_quote: Organ-Anchored Cross-Modal Alignment (OCA) performs fine-grained alignment by using each organ node as a query over the radiology report to selectively aggregate relevant textual evidence, enhancing organ features while preserving anatomical topology.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: OCA then performs fine-grained, organ-level image–text interaction, enhancing CT-derived organ features with organ-specific cues from the radiology report while preserving the anatomy-driven topology.
claims.reason: Section III.A, page 3.

claims.text: Report-Enhanced Graph-Refinement (REG) uses a large language model to extract explicit invasion statements from the report and injects them as a text node connected only to primary sites and invaded organs, refining the graph without discarding anatomy-based risk connections.
claims.poster_quote: Report-Enhanced Graph-Refinement (REG) uses a large language model to extract explicit invasion statements from the report and injects them as a text node connected only to primary sites and invaded organs, refining the graph without discarding anatomy-based risk connections.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: REG uses a large language model (LLM) to incorporate report-derived invasion statements as a guidance signal on top of AOG, refining the multimodal organ graph without discarding anatomy-based risk connections.
claims.reason: Section III.A, page 3.
